---
title: All platforms
description: Which booking platforms gamexo speaks to today, and what is coming.
---

Three platforms sell court time through gamexo. Each dictates its own integration
contract, so each gets its own adapter — different paths, different field names,
different response envelopes.

| Platform | Status | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Playo](/docs/integrations/third-party/playo) | **Live** | External Venue Integration v2.0 — theirs |
| [Hudle](/docs/integrations/third-party/hudle) | Coming soon | Awaiting their spec |
| [District](/docs/integrations/third-party/district) | Coming soon | Awaiting their spec |
| [gamexo API](/docs/integrations/gamexo-api) | **Live** | Ours — the default |

## Why separate adapters

Folding every platform into one namespace would mean a single endpoint declaring one
response schema while returning several shapes, and each new platform would deepen
the ambiguity. So the adapters stay separate and honest.

What they share is everything that matters. An adapter translates wire format and
nothing else: no adapter decides anything about a booking. Availability, holds,
confirmation, cancellation and every guarantee in
[Core concepts](/docs/integrations/concepts) are one implementation, reached
identically by all of them.

The practical consequence for you: a platform integrated last week and one integrated
today get the same atomicity, the same idempotency and the same expiry behaviour.
There is no "mature" integration and no second-class one.

## If you are not one of these three

Use the [gamexo API](/docs/integrations/gamexo-api). It is the default contract, it is
live, and integrating against it needs nothing built on our side — a venue issues you
a key and you can start.
